findings.title: becoming into class membership
findings.claim: The becoming verb turns the carried-burden event into the addressee entering a defined outcome class.
findings.mechanism: The second-person subjunctive takes the following prepositional predicate, so the same participant who bears the burden is the one who comes into the class.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the result is not another action but entry into a class.
findings.containment: The plain consequence remains intact; class entry is limited to the local becoming-plus-membership construction.

epistemic.reason: The focus-aligned form and typed local support directly establish the bounded relation.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader notices the action turning into an existential status, while broader formation and place senses remain only pressure.
findings.containment: The ordinary becoming remains primary; broader formation and place associations are pressure on the word, not separate local claims.
